experiments.scope: The blake3-r6-prefix-v1 target with 128-byte messages P || K || x (P the fixed first block, K the fixed 32-byte prefix of block 2, two blocks, flags 1 then 10), collision of the low 18 bits of the complete digest. Each trial runs ONE attempt of the shipped 256-lane search on the walk g = f XOR q (plan(18): distinguished points with the low 2 bits all ones, 8 batches of 256 lanes, the stage-1 test, the quotient-filter table, the cut rule, the recovery with checkpoints on the packed circuit) from a word derived from the trial seed, with no amplification, and returns the two 128-byte messages P || K || x and P || K || y when the attempt found a pair, two nulls otherwise. The same program also runs the same attempt on an ideal function of the same width (keyed blake2b) and one family-law run with a fresh prefix at n = 12; these are reported as untrusted observations only.
experiments.hypothesis: For every returned pair the two messages are distinct and their complete 6-round digests agree in the low 18 bits (digest bytes 0 and 1 and the low 2 bits of byte 2). This is exact: the program recovers a merge of two trails of the walk g = f XOR q at width 18. The number of trials that return a pair is reported as a program check, with the ideal-function control as an untrusted observation, and no probability, interval or sampling inference is drawn from it. Observations (untrusted, the program's own): target_ok, ideal_ok, target_batches, target_halt, ideal_halt, t1_steps. Not shown: any width-256 cost or success probability. Before any trial the program asserts that the generated step has 37220 gates = 36872 fixed + the scan objective 348 of P_INDEX (proof 3.2, 3.7), so the organizer's run of either experiment also checks the step's gate count and the prefix price; a failed assertion fails the run.

experiments.scope: The blake3-r6-prefix-v1 target with 128-byte messages P || K || x at full width 256. Each trial evaluates 1024 points x with the shipped bit-sliced circuit (source by trial index mod 3: uniform inputs from the seed, counter inputs r + i, iterates of g from 256 seed-derived starts), recovers the digests from the stored planes by XOR with q, and returns the two 128-byte messages of two distinct points whose complete digests agree in the low 20 bits when the set contains such a pair, two nulls otherwise. Untrusted observations: the source and the number of equal pairs in the low 20 bits.
experiments.hypothesis: For every returned pair the two messages P || K || x and P || K || y are distinct and their complete 6-round digests agree in the low 20 bits (digest bytes 0 and 1 and the low 4 bits of byte 2). This is exact: it checks the bit-sliced circuit, the mask q and the two-block message construction at full width. The number of returned pairs and the equal-pair counts are reported as program checks, not as estimates, and no inference is drawn from them. Observations (untrusted): source, dup_w0. Not shown: collision structure at 2^128 evaluations. Before any trial the program asserts that the generated step has 37220 gates = 36872 fixed + the scan objective 348 of P_INDEX (proof 3.2, 3.7), so the organizer's run of either experiment also checks the step's gate count and the prefix price; a failed assertion fails the run.
